_comment: This repository's record of the loop-kit files it has deliberately repaired.
Read by tests/test_kit_manifest.py; written by hand, in the commit that makes
the repair. QUESTIONS.md Q-27, answered 'enforce it here' by the operator on
KIT_MANIFEST.json beside this file is NOT this file's business: install-kit.ps1
owns it, writes it on every install, and uses it to tell a safe update from a
local edit. Re-baselining it to the working tree is the bug its own comment
records (three prove_fail.py repairs clobbered, 2026-08-23 04:35). This file is
separate so a repair can be recorded without touching the installer's state.
kit_version is the kit these entries were dispositioned against. When an
install moves KIT_VERSION, the test goes red until every entry below has been
re-checked against the kit that replaced it: one the kit has absorbed loses its
entry, one it has not keeps it with a fresh hash. That is the version
discipline Q-27's answer asked for, and the moment a repair can go upstream.
sha256 is over the file's raw bytes, matching install-kit.ps1's Sha256. The
kit's own manifest.json uses canonical LF bytes instead; the two are different

.claude/agents/auditor.md.why:
Q-46, answered 'fix the auditor and quarantine the report' by the operator on 2026-09-03, adds a seventh repair: the FINDINGS rules now forbid opening a Finding cell with `**Claim as first raised in report NNN**:` and dating a finding by its ID label at all - the practice abolished at report 107 (CQ-236) and guarded by `tests/test_a_finding_is_not_dated_by_a_reused_label.py`, which report 139 (170 annotations) reddened for three rounds at preflight. The report is quarantined by name in the guard rather than edited; the prohibition is here so the set of quarantined reports never grows. GENERIC: any consumer whose labels were once renumbered has the same trap, and the rule belongs upstream beside the carry-note rule. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry.

Round 133 adds a sixth repair, WF-90's half of the fix: step 4b, having asked whether the audit window's read of `OPERATOR_ACTIONS.md` is complete for RESTARTS, now asks the same of BUILDS by running `scripts/check_builds.py`. A restart changes which Python the process holds; `npm run build` changes what the browser is served, and the register is equally where a round looks to find out. Measured: at `712743b` the register's newest bundle is `BsBHgXUu` while `index-BsXucSZn.js` sat on disk dated later, served by a process started before it, and the string does not appear in the file at all -- the commit body mentions that build in prose and the register does not, and the register is what the loop reads. Nothing compared the two for the fifty-nine reports between 074 and 132: `grep -rn` over every `.py` under `scripts/`, `tests/` and `clauditseo/` on 2026-09-01 returned only docstring prose, the two rendered-a11y modules that LOAD the bundle to drive a browser, and `prove_fail.py`, which detects those. GENERIC in shape for the same reason the round-130 restart repair is: any repo the kit installs into that serves a built front end can rebuild it without recording the rebuild, and the check takes its asset directory from the profile's `build_dir` rather than from anything about this board. Unlike the restart check it takes no `--since` -- the built directory is cleaned on every build, so it carries the name of exactly one build and there is no window to bound. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry.

Round 131 adds a fifth repair, WF-96's half of the fix: the step that tells the auditor to re-read a carried row's claim against the code now says to read the row's stated CONSEQUENCE and not only its lead sentence, because the lead sentence is usually not the claim. Measured: of the 176 rows `check_anchors.py --context` emits from report 131, 172 lead with a carry note -- an account of whether the anchor moved since the last report -- so the instruction as written pointed the reader at the one cell of a carried row that says nothing about the code. UX-09 is the case the whole flag exists for and the case it could not have caught: three days after `ca8c02c` repaired it, `--context` printed `UX-09 (High) -- Carried, unchanged bytes.` and the row was carried at High for twenty-eight consecutive reports. GENERIC in shape: any repo the kit installs into carries findings across reports, and the carry note is a property of how a carried row is written rather than of this board -- the paired `scripts/check_anchors.py` change is generic for the same reason and belongs upstream with it. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry.

Round 130 adds a fourth repair, WF-47's half of the fix: step 4b, having bounded the read of `OPERATOR_ACTIONS.md` to the audit window, now asks whether that window is COMPLETE by running `scripts/check_restarts.py --since <previous audit commit>`. Until this, the instruction to read the register before concluding a finding is fixed was only as good as the register, and the register was measurably short -- 15 of 136 recorded starts had no row within fifteen minutes, 7 of them with no marker at all. GENERIC in shape: any repo the kit installs into whose product records its own restarts has the same gap, and the auditor everywhere is told to trust a hand-written register. What is NOT generic is the reader -- `check_restarts.py` reads `clauditseo/provenance.py`'s own constant -- so an upstream version would take the register's path from the consumer's profile. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. The auditor's read of the two growing registers is bounded and their aged tails rotated (a388683, 2026-08-30), and the anchor gate shows the claim beside the code (2ee1257, 2026-08-23). Both are repairs to how this repo's audit reads this repo's registers; whether the bound belongs upstream is a kit judgement, not settled here. Round 120 adds a third, independent repair: step 5 runs the suite through `scripts/run-suite.ps1` so a red audit run leaves its assertion text on disk. Round 120 wires the pinned suite through `scripts/run-suite.ps1` so a red run's assertion text survives (CQ-237, QUESTIONS.md Q-36). The wrapper adds no flags -- it reads `suite_command` out of PROFILE.md at run time -- so this is not a change to what green means; what changes is that the run is still readable afterwards. Generic: every repo the kit installs into runs its suite through a tool whose output is truncated above the failure section, and none of them can currently say which assertion fired. This one belongs upstream with the check_anchors repair rather than with the model-by-depth one. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry.

.claude/skills/audit-fix/SKILL.md.why: The auditor's model follows the audit depth (aed54ac, 2026-08-29), the register-rotation lever was added (a388683) and then dropped again when the operator answered Q-33 (3eb3d1f, 2026-08-31). Relay item 120 then ported kit 1.11.0's gather-step bound onto this copy by hand — the operator's answer to Q-35, 2026-08-31, made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. After that port the divergence runs in both directions deliberately: the bound came from the kit, while the model-by-depth choice, the pre-audit fresh-crawl procedure and the `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` section bound are this repo's. The model-by-depth choice is general and is the piece to lift upstream; the rotation history is local churn that upstream never saw and should not inherit. Round 120 adds the suite-capture repair at both places a round runs the pinned suite -- preflight step 5 and step 5 Verify. Round 120 wires the pinned suite through `scripts/run-suite.ps1` so a red run's assertion text survives (CQ-237, QUESTIONS.md Q-36). The wrapper adds no flags -- it reads `suite_command` out of PROFILE.md at run time -- so this is not a change to what green means; what changes is that the run is still readable afterwards. Generic: every repo the kit installs into runs its suite through a tool whose output is truncated above the failure section, and none of them can currently say which assertion fired. This one belongs upstream with the check_anchors repair rather than with the model-by-depth one. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. Relay item 122 adds a fourth divergence, and it is a deletion of local authority rather than an addition: step 5's **Red** bullet no longer says what a red means on its own account, it defers to DISCIPLINE rule 6, which now owns the re-run carve-out (Q-39, answered 2026-09-01). Travels with the DISCIPLINE.md entry or not at all -- the bullet cites a rule that must exist. Relay item 122, 2026-09-01, records `QUESTIONS.md` Q-39's answer -- *only where the cause is known load-related* -- in the one place every skill reads. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. Relay item 125 adds a fifth divergence, of the same deferring kind as the fourth: step 5 Verify gains a **Red** bullet where it had only a **Passes** one, and that bullet decides nothing on its own account -- it points at rule 6, which now reaches verify. Without it the step a round reads at the moment the answer applies is silent. Travels with the DISCIPLINE.md entry or not at all. -- Round 132 adds the preflight read that runs `scripts/check_carveout.py` bounded to the previous audit commit, beside the baseline the same step takes -- WF-98, report 132. Placed at preflight and not at step 5 because the subject is the reds ALREADY on disk from previous rounds, not this round's own; and stated as a read rather than a gate, so it cannot stop a round over a record another round wrote. Same shape as the `check_restarts.py` read `auditor.md` step 4b carries, and the same disclaimer: an unquoted red is a question, not a verdict. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. 2026-09-06, Q-48: the two `**Red**` bullets said a green re-run of the unchanged tree is what may clear a red, and named the filed load-sensitive class as the bound. Both are now false. They defer to rule 6 as before -- the property `tests/test_loop_instructions.py` guards is that a skill points at the rule rather than restating it -- and what they say ABOUT the rule now matches it: the question is whether the node reproduces alone, and the carve-out asks for three things rather than one.

.claude/skills/backlog-plan/SKILL.md.why: Round 130 adds a second divergence, the other half of WF-47: the *Every register the loop keeps* table gains the two rows it was missing, `QUESTIONS.md` and `data/server-starts.jsonl`. That table states its own purpose -- 'a register added to the loop is a row added here' -- and had no guard, so it had missed two by the time anything checked; `tests/test_every_register_the_loop_keeps_has_a_row_in_the_planner_table.py` now derives the population from the tree rather than from a list, and failed against the unfixed table naming both. GENERIC: the table and its promise are the kit's, and so is the failure mode of a promise nothing enforces. The derived population is half local -- root Markdown is the kit's shape, `data/server-starts.jsonl` is this product's. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. A price in the ledger says what put it there (294e98d, 2026-08-23). This one predates the kit 1.3.0 install at 06cd719 and was already a CONFLICT when it ran, so the installer correctly kept the earlier hash rather than the local one - the entry has never matched the tree in this repository, which is why the drift read as seven rather than five.

.claude/skills/feature/SKILL.md.why: First divergence in this file. Its preflight runs the pinned suite and now runs it through `scripts/run-suite.ps1`. Round 120 wires the pinned suite through `scripts/run-suite.ps1` so a red run's assertion text survives (CQ-237, QUESTIONS.md Q-36). The wrapper adds no flags -- it reads `suite_command` out of PROFILE.md at run time -- so this is not a change to what green means; what changes is that the run is still readable afterwards. Generic: every repo the kit installs into runs its suite through a tool whose output is truncated above the failure section, and none of them can currently say which assertion fired. This one belongs upstream with the check_anchors repair rather than with the model-by-depth one. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry.

scripts/check_anchors.py.why:
0853bcf (2026-09-14) adds a repair to `tree_basenames`: a directory holding its own `.git` (a file, for a git worktree) is pruned like `.git` itself. A parallel Claude session's `.claude/worktrees/*` checkout appeared mid-suite, duplicated every filename, and `test_every_bare_source_citation_that_names_a_file_resolves` resolved nothing. GENERIC: any repo the kit installs into can grow a nested worktree the same way, and the fix takes nothing from this board. Round 131 repairs WF-96 where the finding is: `context_lines` labelled each row with `_claim(cells[2])`, the first sentence of the Finding cell, and now prints the row's `Impact` cell beside it as `  consequence: ...`. Measured on report 131: 172 of the 176 rows the flag emits lead with a carry note rather than a claim, 97%, one of the two Highs among them -- so the reading surface built to catch a repaired row was showing, for almost every row, an account of whether the anchor moved instead of anything about the code. On UX-09's row in report 043, three days after `ca8c02c` repaired it, the printed line was `UX-09 (High) -- Carried, unchanged bytes.`; the Impact cell on the same row read "The line written to make the document honest is its least readable sentence" and was never printed. This decides nothing and adds no matcher -- round 129 measured two candidate semantic matchers for the sibling source-comment problem and rejected both -- it prints one more cell the report already wrote. GENERIC: every repo the kit installs into carries rows across reports and opens a carried row with a carry note, so this belongs upstream with the earlier `check_anchors.py` repairs. Watched failing by `tests/test_a_carried_row_is_read_by_more_than_its_carry_note.py`, which named all 176 rows before the change. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry.

Round 130 adds a seventh, WF-48: `register_anchor_paths` located its anchor and finding columns by exact membership in the header cells, so the strike test ran only where a header read exactly `finding`. Measured on this register, 116 of 172 anchor-bearing rows sat under 44 other spellings -- `findings in report 044`, `finding behind it` -- and had no strike test at all, so a path went quiet in the cohort gate the day the loop finished the work on it. Both lookups are now `^anchors?\b` / `^findings?\b`; the anchor one had no defect yet and moves with its sibling because they implement one rule. GENERIC, and among the plainest here: the column spellings are the kit's own derived-table convention, and the defect is in kit code with no ClauditSEO content in it. The live set is unchanged for this register as it stands -- no derived row is currently struck -- and `tests/test_a_struck_row_is_honoured_in_every_table_shape_the_register_uses.py` asserts that rather than leaving it remembered. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. Five repairs to the anchor gate: the claim shown beside the code (2ee1257), source-comment addresses checked against a walked tree (7678fa5, CQ-151), an anchor under generated output is not an address (2b49fcd), a duplicate count says what it stopped counting (e3427ee, CQ-230), bare source citations resolved with ambiguity reddening (1f3d8c0, Q-28), and the listing surviving the characters a report is written in (round 116, CQ-234 - made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry). Six repairs now. The most-repaired kit file here and the strongest candidate to lift upstream, and CQ-234 is the plainest of them: a `print` that raises `UnicodeEncodeError` on a piped Windows stdout is a defect on every repo the kit installs into, not a ClauditSEO one.

scripts/round-marker.ps1.why: A phase update keeps the kind it found (294e98d, 2026-08-23), guarded by tests/test_a_phase_update_keeps_the_kind_it_found.py. Like backlog-plan/SKILL.md this predates the 1.3.0 install and was carried through it as a conflict. A correctness fix to a shared tool: it belongs upstream.

scripts/timings-append.ps1.why: The golden score reaches a tracked register (c54b57b, relay 087, 2026-08-24). Adds a section this repo's TIMINGS.md has; whether the kit's template has it is an upstream question.

tests/test_loop_instructions.py.why:
2026-09-22 (item 187, the public-tree scrub): the register files this guard reads are no longer guaranteed to be in the tree it runs in. `PUBLIC_EXCLUDE.txt` keeps the operator's working record out of the public export - `audits/`, `OPERATOR_ACTIONS.md`, `TIMINGS.md`, `NEXT_UP.md` - and four of this file's clauses read them. Two changes: `PRESENT_REGISTERS` narrows the TABLE_FILES parametrisation to the register files that exist, so the table-shape guards still cover `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` in a tree carrying no `audits/`; and `test_every_register_named_exists`, `test_the_scan_reaches_the_audit_reports` and the two set-counting clauses carry `tests/private_register.needs_register`, which skips with a stated reason rather than failing. `REGISTER_FILES` itself is untouched: that the WRITTEN list is honest is exactly what the first of those clauses is about, and narrowing it would have made that clause vacuous. Measured before the change: a fresh export of the tree could not COLLECT the suite at all - one module-level read of an absent audit report aborted all 4,200 tests - and after it, the exported tree runs clean with those guards skipping. GENERIC: any repo the kit installs into may publish a subset of itself, and a kit guard that reads a register the subset omits has this problem wherever it lands; the shape that belongs upstream is "narrow the parametrisation to what exists, skip the existence guard, and never read a register at import time". What is NOT generic is the manifest's path, which an upstream version would take from the consumer's profile. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry.

2026-09-14: `INSTRUCTION_FILES` skips any `.md` under a directory holding its own `.git`, the same rule `scripts/check_anchors.py`'s index gained in 0853bcf. A parallel session's `.claude/worktrees/*` checkout sits under `.claude/`, so its whole tree - audit reports included - joined the instruction scope and reddened 29 nodes. GENERIC: the kit's glob over .claude/ meets any worktree made there. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. The guard that the auditor's model matches the audit depth (aed54ac, 2026-08-29), the assertion half of the audit-fix/SKILL.md repair above; those two move together and should be lifted together. Round 116 adds a second, independent repair (CQ-234's sibling CQ-233, in the commit this hash was written into): the bare-carriage-return scan gains the detector clause the BOM scan has had since round 039, plus an assertion that the scan reaches `audits/` at all. That half is generic - it is about this file's own guards, not about ClauditSEO - and belongs upstream with the check_anchors repair rather than with the model-by-depth one. Relay item 122 adds `test_the_re_run_carve_out_is_stated_once` and `test_every_red_bullet_defers_to_the_rule_rather_than_restating_it`: the Q-39 carve-out is stated in `.claude/DISCIPLINE.md` and nowhere else, and every `**Red**` bullet in the tree cites rule 6 rather than restating it. Both were run red against the unfixed instructions before the fix landed. Populations derived from the tree -- `INSTRUCTION_FILES` and a pattern over the bullets -- so a second skill growing its own copy is inside the checked set. Generic in shape and specific in its marker phrase; it travels upstream with the DISCIPLINE.md entry or not at all. Relay item 122, 2026-09-01, records `QUESTIONS.md` Q-39's answer -- *only where the cause is known load-related* -- in the one place every skill reads. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. Relay item 125 adds `test_the_carve_out_says_what_a_red_verifying_run_means` and `test_no_instruction_file_re_opens_the_answered_verify_question`: rule 6's carve-out section must decide the verify case rather than record it as unanswered, and no instruction file may still send a round to ask a question the operator has answered. The second was run red against the unfixed instructions -- two hits, both in `.claude/DISCIPLINE.md`; the first is a floor rather than a proof and its docstring says so. The population is `INSTRUCTION_FILES`, derived from the tree. Travels upstream with the DISCIPLINE.md entry or not at all. 2026-09-06, Q-48: `CARVE_OUT_MARKER` is the handle every carve-out guard uses to find the section, and the section's heading changed with the mechanism -- "A red the re-run clears" became "A red that will not reproduce". The guards themselves are untouched: one owner for the rule, and the section must still decide the verify case. Q-48 moved what the rule says, not where it lives. 2026-09-24, the exported tree: `_tracked_text_files` now skips its callers where the tree has no `.git`, through `tests/needs_repo.py`, instead of raising `CalledProcessError` on `git ls-files`. The public export of 7f0c450 failed three tests here, each `fatal: not a git repository`. The raise-not-narrow rule is untouched: a skip scans nothing and passes nothing, and git missing from a real repository still fails. Generic: any repo the kit installs into can be exported or downloaded as a zip. Travels upstream only with `tests/needs_repo.py`.

.claude/DISCIPLINE.md.why: First divergence in this file. Relay item 122, 2026-09-01, records `QUESTIONS.md` Q-39's answer -- *only where the cause is known load-related* -- in the one place every skill reads. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. Rule 6 gains the baseline carve-out: a green re-run of an unchanged tree may stand as a round's step-5 baseline only where the failing node is in the filed load-sensitive class (`KNOWN_ISSUES.md` KI-22 and KI-51, named as the register rather than copied as a list), any other red stops the round, and the carve-out is bounded to the baseline -- a red verifying run still blocks the commit. Rule 6 rather than a skill because this file's own header records what two copies of one rule cost here. GENERIC, and the strongest of the three for upstream: every repo the kit installs into has a pinned suite that can go red intermittently, and none of them currently says whether a green re-run is a baseline. What is NOT generic is the class itself -- KI-22 and KI-51 are ClauditSEO rows -- so an upstream version would name the consumer's own known-issues register instead. Q-40 is where that decision lives. Relay item 125, 2026-09-01, records `QUESTIONS.md` Q-42's answer -- *extend the carve-out to verify, on the same terms* -- in the same rule. Rule 6's closing paragraph had bounded the carve-out to the baseline and said in terms that verify was unanswered; that sentence is replaced by the extension, on the baseline's own three conditions (filed load-sensitive class, both `.claude/run/` paths quoted, membership judged by cause) and no looser ones, with the cost the operator accepted written beside it. Generic on the same reading as the Q-39 half above and travels with it: every repo the kit installs into has a verifying run that can go red intermittently, and a stall there is worse than one at preflight because the tree is already dirty. What is not generic remains the class itself. -- Round 132 adds the check for rule 6's own conditions, WF-98 (report 132). Rule 6 has required a red's `.claude/run/` path since relay 122 and both paths at verify since round 131, and NOTHING COMPARED THE TWO RECORDS -- so a carve-out taken outside the stated conditions left no trace anyone could find. `scripts/check_carveout.py` puts the captures beside the commit bodies; this entry is the paragraph in rule 6 that names it, states its exit codes, and repeats that an unquoted red is a question rather than a verdict. Measured on the first run: 45 captured runs, 14 red and 2 no-result, 11 of them quoted by no commit anywhere, and 6 reds naming no node KI-22/KI-51 files. GENERIC in shape and NOT generic in its register: every repo the kit installs into has a pinned suite that can go red and a rule about it, but KI-22 and KI-51 are ClauditSEO rows, so an upstream port would take the comparison and read the class from the local profile. Made in the commit this hash was written into, whose SHA the entry cannot carry. Relay-adjacent directed work, 2026-09-06, records `QUESTIONS.md` Q-48's answer: rule 6's carve-out is decided by whether a red REPRODUCES when the failing node is run alone, not by whether that node is in a filed class, and the full-suite green re-run is no longer required at all. A red may stand aside only where the round shows three things in the commit body -- the node passes alone on the unchanged tree, the diff cannot reach it at file level, and the round names the class it claims and says whether it suspects its own diff. Verify is reached on the same terms, which is unchanged from relay 125's entry; only the mechanism moved. What decided it is written into the rule rather than only into the answer: four pinned runs over one unchanged tree produced NINE distinct failing nodes with not one repeated, all green serially, so filing by node cannot work (one sitting added eight names to a row that had three); and none of the four was green, so the green re-run every earlier option leaned on is a coin flip whose bias is the machine's load. The counter-example that keeps the suite trustworthy is in the rule too: a real defect in the same sitting -- a stale bundle -- failed alone and kept failing alone, which is exactly what the first clause tests. GENERIC, and more so than what it replaces: the old wording had to name a consumer's own known-issues register (Q-40's open decision), and reproduction needs no register at all, so an upstream version is the same text with nothing to substitute.
